name: Tracking difference
meaning: One-period return lead or lag relative to a benchmark.
commonMistake: Reversing the subtraction order or calling the result tracking error.

name: Custom benchmark return
meaning: Weighted return of benchmark components.
commonMistake: Using weights that do not sum to 100%.

name: Relative return
meaning: Portfolio performance measured against a specified comparator.
workedExample: A 7% portfolio versus 9% benchmark has −2% relative return.
commonMistake: Comparing different periods, currencies, or return conventions.

name: Future value with simple interest
meaning: Principal earns interest but prior interest does not.
commonMistake: Compounding when simple interest is specified.

name: Future value of a single cash flow
meaning: Moves one present cash flow forward through compound growth.
commonMistake: Mismatching the frequency of r and N.

name: Present value of a single cash flow
meaning: Discounts one future cash flow to today.
workedExample: 10,000 in 6 years at 7% is worth 6,663.42 today.
commonMistake: Multiplying instead of dividing when moving backward.

name: Discount factor
meaning: Present value today of one unit received at period N.
workedExample: At 7% for 6 years, the factor is 0.666342.
commonMistake: Using a positive exponent in the numerator.

name: Effective annual rate
meaning: Actual one-year compound growth from a stated rate.
commonMistake: Using the annual stated rate as the periodic rate.

name: Stated annual rate from EAR
meaning: Nominal annual quote consistent with an EAR and compounding frequency.
workedExample: 10.25% EAR with semiannual compounding corresponds to 10% stated.
commonMistake: Multiplying EAR directly by m.

name: Continuous-compounding future value
meaning: Future value when compounding is continuous.
commonMistake: Using the discrete compound formula.

name: Continuous-compounding present value
meaning: Discounts a future cash flow continuously.
workedExample: 1,000 due in 2 years at 5% has PV 904.84.
commonMistake: Forgetting the negative exponent.

name: PV of multiple cash flows
meaning: Sums individually discounted cash flows at a common date.
commonMistake: Adding cash flows before accounting for their different dates.

name: PV of ordinary annuity
meaning: Value today of equal end-of-period payments.
workedExample: Five year-end payments of 1,000 at 6% are worth 4,212.36.
commonMistake: Using BGN timing for end-of-period payments.

name: FV of ordinary annuity
meaning: Accumulated value of equal end-of-period payments.
workedExample: Four year-end deposits of 2,000 at 5% grow to 8,620.25.
commonMistake: Giving the final payment an extra period of growth.

name: Annuity due value
meaning: Adjusts an ordinary annuity because every payment occurs one period earlier.

variables.Value ordinary: PV or FV for end payments

workedExample: 8,620.25 ordinary FV at 5% becomes 9,051.26 due FV.
commonMistake: Using BGN mode and multiplying again.

name: PV of level perpetuity
meaning: Value of equal payments continuing forever, first paid next period.
commonMistake: Treating a payment today as part of the formula.

name: PV of growing perpetuity
meaning: Value of perpetual cash flows growing at constant g, with r greater than g.
commonMistake: Using today's cash flow or allowing g to equal/exceed r.

name: PV of growing annuity
meaning: Value of a finite stream with constant payment growth.
commonMistake: Using an infinite-perpetuity result for a finite stream.

name: Amortizing loan payment
meaning: Equal end-of-period payment that fully amortizes a loan.
workedExample: 20,000 for 4 annual payments at 6% requires 5,771.83 per year.
commonMistake: Using annual N with a monthly rate.

name: Loan payment decomposition
expression: Interest = Beginning balance × r; Principal = PMT − Interest
meaning: Splits an amortizing payment into financing cost and debt reduction.
workedExample: On 20,000 at 6%, first interest is 1,200 and 4,571.83 reduces principal.
commonMistake: Calculating interest on ending balance.

name: Fixed-rate bond value
meaning: Sum of coupon-annuity PV and principal PV.
workedExample: Three 50 coupons plus 1,000 principal at 6% are worth 973.27.
commonMistake: Omitting principal or mixing annual and semiannual inputs.

name: Inflation-adjusted future target
meaning: Future currency amount needed to preserve today's purchasing power.
commonMistake: Discounting when the task is to inflate a current real target forward.

name: Price-weighted index level
meaning: Measures a price-weighted basket while the divisor preserves continuity.
intuition: Measures a price-weighted basket while the divisor preserves continuity.
commonMistake: Adjust the divisor for splits.
relatedLearningOutcome: calculate and compare money-weighted and time-weighted rates of return

name: Equal-weighted index return
meaning: Gives each constituent equal beginning weight.
intuition: Gives each constituent equal beginning weight.
commonMistake: Periodic rebalancing is required.
relatedLearningOutcome: calculate and compare money-weighted and time-weighted rates of return

name: Capitalization-weighted index return
meaning: Weights constituents by beginning market value.
intuition: Weights constituents by beginning market value.
commonMistake: Use beginning weights.
relatedLearningOutcome: calculate and compare money-weighted and time-weighted rates of return

name: Float-adjusted capitalization
meaning: Excludes strategic or restricted holdings from investable capitalization.
intuition: Excludes strategic or restricted holdings from investable capitalization.
workedExample: Market value 800 and float factor 60% gives 480.
commonMistake: Do not apply the float factor twice.
relatedLearningOutcome: calculate and compare money-weighted and time-weighted rates of return

name: Implied forward interest rate

variables.f_1,1: one-year forward rate one year ahead

meaning: Uses no-arbitrage across maturities.
commonMistake: Match compounding conventions.
relatedLearningOutcome: calculate and interpret the present value of fixed-income and equity instruments based on expected future cash flows

name: No-arbitrage forward exchange rate
meaning: Links the forward quotation to relative financing rates.
intuition: Links the forward quotation to relative financing rates.
commonMistake: Keep the quotation direction consistent.
relatedLearningOutcome: calculate and interpret the present value of fixed-income and equity instruments based on expected future cash flows

name: Implied constant equity growth
meaning: Rearranges the constant-growth valuation model.
commonMistake: Use the next dividend, not the last dividend.
relatedLearningOutcome: calculate and interpret the present value of fixed-income and equity instruments based on expected future cash flows

name: Put–call parity
meaning: Equates portfolios with identical expiration payoffs.
intuition: Equates portfolios with identical expiration payoffs.
workedExample: If S0=100, p=6, and PV(X)=95, call value is 11.
commonMistake: Options must share strike and expiration.
relatedLearningOutcome: calculate and interpret the present value of fixed-income and equity instruments based on expected future cash flows
